items.title: Jon Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 17, 2003 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And the executive producer, Steve Phillips, said he really highly respects Max Roach and he said well yeah let’s do it.

ctx.x: Well I don’t run the record company. I co-founded the record company and it gave an opportunity for many Asian American artists to self produce a recording and try to use it to leverage themselves to create more work opportunities. But it’s changed where, I mean now in Chicago somebody else is handling the business. We have a catalogue I think of over 60 recordings, maybe 70 by now. But I co-founded it. So my relationship with the record company was after Soul Note, their recording projects diminished and I…

great relationship with Max Roach at that time and he just he got the MacArthur and so it was great developing that relationship. But I hadn’t done anything with him, I think it was, yeah it was seven or eight years. And so here was an opportunity, would you like to record with Max Roach. I said well I’ll see what Max has to say. So I’m thinking well okay maybe in three or five years I’ll be able to raise the money and be able to do that. And when I told Max in May 1998, I was in New York with James Newton doing…
Wow. When people ask you what you do, if they don’t know you too well, what do you say?
